Overview

re-psn answers the matchmaking and leaderboard calls of a statically recompiled PS3 game, for a group running its own server: a LAN, a VPN, or friends connecting to one person's machine. The server keeps rooms and leaderboards and tells each player where the others are. Game traffic goes directly between players, and through the server only when two players cannot reach each other and the host has turned the relay on.

It is a fork of psnr by sp00nz: a Go server and a one-file C client, with no accounts and no public instance.

Version 0.4.0 (pre-release). 64 features: 29 available, 3 not yet verified, 7 partial, 15 planned, 9 later, 1 declined.

Unofficial; not affiliated with Sony. No game files, keys or firmware are in the repository or needed from it. Play only games you own.

Features

One row per feature. A status rests on a test or a recorded run in the repository; the features page has the evidence for each row.

Rooms and matchmaking

FeatureStatusSince
Rooms and search rooms-basic
Create, search, join and leave rooms modelled on sceNpMatching2. A search sees only the rooms of its own title, with each room's external data. Room messages, owner kicks, owner handoff when the owner leaves, and member pushes with each peer's address and P2P port.
Upstream work. KICK_MEMBER removes a member but does not prevent rejoining.		available0.1.0
Room and member data rooms-data
External and internal room data (only the owner writes it), room flags that searchers see (SET_ROOM_DATA which 2), and member data sent with CREATE_ROOM and JOIN_ROOM and returned in every member entry.
External and internal data are upstream work (0.1.0). Room flags and member data are newer, so clients built against 0.1.0 no longer match.		available0.2.0
Invite-only rooms rooms-codes
An 8-character code per room (SET_ROOM_ACCESS, JOIN_BY_CODE, GET_ROOM_ACCESS). The room leaves search and the status page, which counts unlisted rooms. A connection that sends too many wrong codes is closed.
Protocol 0.4: HELLO_ACK flags bit 1 says the server has them. Codes are never logged.		available0.2.0
Private rooms rooms-private
Matching2 room passwords, private slots and join by room ID. A relay-only variant that keeps members' addresses hidden from each other is also wanted.
The relay-only variant is not designed yet.		plannednot released

Leaderboards

FeatureStatusSince
Leaderboards scores-boards
Modelled on sceNpScore: each player's best score is kept, a tie goes to whoever scored first, boards are higher-is-better or lower-is-better, and ranks are read by range or by online ID.
Upstream work. Kept in memory: a restart empties every board. Opt-in storage is planned (store-sqlite).		available0.1.0

Players

FeatureStatusSince
One player per name players-names
Names are compared case-insensitively. A HELLO with a name held from another address gets ERROR 8 (name taken); from the same address it is the same player reconnecting, and the old connection is closed.
No passwords: a name is not authenticated.		available0.2.0
Friends, presence and invites players-friends
sceNpBasic: a friends list (everyone on the same server), presence (online, title, room), invites and join-a-friend, player history and a block list.
Not in the server today.		plannednot released
Optional sign-in players-accounts
Optional accounts next to the default of a name per player: a credential per server kept on the player's machine, sign-in through a generic OpenID Connect provider, or with Discord or GitHub.
Not started. Needs the opt-in database (store-sqlite) first, and the scope in ROADMAP.md says no accounts or passwords, so that needs changing too. The default would stay a name per player.		laternot released

Limits

FeatureStatusSince
Request and connection limits limits-requests
-max-rooms, -max-player-rooms, -max-conns-per-addr, -max-req-rate (requests per second per connection) and a size cap on room data. A request over a limit is refused; a connection over the rate is closed. Each refusal is logged at warn level.
These limits cover TCP. Main also has bounded UDP admission and drop counters; see the partial net-guardrails row.		available0.2.0

Logging

FeatureStatusSince
Log levels and formats logs-levels
-log-level (debug, info, warn, error), -v as debug, -log-format text or json, and -log-file to append to a file (mode 0600). Connection and room refusals are logged at warn level; UDP drops use aggregate counters, with one warning per player for a mismatched probe. Tokens and query strings are never logged.
Not checked: no test covers -log-file. The server does not rotate the file.		available0.2.0

Status page

FeatureStatusSince
Status page and /api/stats, with a token status-page
A read-only page and JSON on a separate listener, off unless -http names an address (127.0.0.1:36101 keeps it on localhost). -http-token requires a token (Authorization: Bearer, or ?token=), and the server warns at start when the page is reachable from elsewhere without one. Since v0.4.0 the page uses gruvbox-material, Rooms/Leaderboards tabs, System/Light/Dark and browser-local text size, spacing and contrast-checked custom colours.
The page and /api/stats are upstream work (0.1.0); the token is the fork's.		available0.2.0

Reverse proxy

FeatureStatusSince
PROXY protocol and trusted proxies proxy-support
-trusted-proxies (CIDRs or addresses) and -proxy-protocol (a PROXY v1 or v2 header required on the game TCP port from a listed proxy), and forwarded headers for the status page log. The real client address then counts for the limits, the name rule, public_ip and the log.
Off by default. UDP is not proxied. See docs/running.md.		available0.2.0

Deployment

FeatureStatusSince

deploy/ holds re-psn.env.example (every setting, commented), a systemd unit and a Traefik config that sends PROXY v2. The release archives carry them as examples/.
scripts/check-deploy.sh checks the env file and the unit against the server's flags. The Traefik run (Traefik 3.1 under Podman) is recorded in docs/running.md; no run of the systemd unit is recorded.		available0.2.0
nginx and HAProxy examples deploy-nginx-haproxy
An nginx stream block with proxy_protocol on; (PROXY v1) and an HAProxy config with send-proxy-v2.
Not checked: neither config has been run against the server (docs/running.md says so).		not yet verified0.2.0
Caddy status-page example deploy-caddy
A stock Caddy 2 HTTP reverse-proxy example in deploy/caddy/, copied into future release archives with the other deployment examples. Defaults to loopback and leaves game TCP/UDP direct.
Written from the official Caddy documentation; not run or validated with Caddy. No layer-4 plugin is included. The existing HTTP token check is preserved and client-supplied CF-Connecting-IP is removed before forwarding.		not yet verified0.4.0
Optional fail2ban status-token jail deploy-fail2ban
A disabled systemd-journal filter/jail example for repeated HTTP status-token refusals. Uses JSON logs and a host TCP status-port action, with setup, firewall placement, validation and recovery instructions.
Offline synthetic HTTP/logger and native fail2ban-engine checks do not establish live journal/firewall enforcement. Game TCP/UDP, proxy/CDN and bridged-container enforcement are outside the sample's scope; install and verify fail2ban separately.		not yet verified0.4.0
Docker and Podman deploy-container
A two-stage Dockerfile and a compose file in docker/, configured only by RE_PSN_* variables. The status page is off until RE_PSN_HTTP is set.
A Podman 6.1 run is recorded in docker/README.md, and the NAT lab builds the image with Docker in CI. The v0.2.0 image is pushed to ghcr.io (amd64 and arm64, unsigned; arm64 not run). The server runs as a non-root user and the bases are pinned by digest. Opt-in host-networking compose files, one hardened for a shared test host, are for Linux only. Compose under Podman is not tested.		available0.2.0

Settings

FeatureStatusSince
Flags and RE_PSN_* variables settings-env
Every flag can be set as RE_PSN_<FLAG>; the old PSNR_<FLAG> names still work as aliases. A flag wins, then RE_PSN_, then PSNR_. An old name logs a warning that names the variables, never the value. -tcp-addr and -udp-addr give the two game sockets their own addresses. A bad value stops the server at start.
No config file yet.		available0.2.0

Storage

FeatureStatusSince
Storage interface store-interface
A storage layer with an in-memory backend, the leaderboards wired through it, and a -db (RE_PSN_DB) setting. Off by default, so nothing changes unless a host turns it on.
Only off and memory exist, so scores are still kept in memory and lost on restart; other schemes stop the start. First step of opt-in storage (store-sqlite is next).		available0.2.0
SQLite storage (opt-in) store-sqlite
An SQLite backend with a pure-Go driver, so the release archives stay static, and migrations built into the binary. With it on, scores survive a restart. The connection string is never logged.
Not started. The server's first third-party Go module. Player names and bans would follow with accounts.		plannednot released
Backup and restore store-backup
Documented backup and restore for each database: a backup command or a copy procedure for SQLite; a dump command with timer and cron examples for PostgreSQL and MariaDB. How long backups are kept is up to the host.
Not started. Comes with store-sqlite.		plannednot released
PostgreSQL storage store-postgres
A PostgreSQL backend for hosts who bring their own database; the server does not run or manage it.
After store-sqlite.		laternot released
MariaDB storage store-mariadb
A MariaDB backend for hosts who bring their own database; the server does not run or manage it.
After store-sqlite.		laternot released

High availability

FeatureStatusSince
Health check and clean restarts ha-restart
A data-free /healthz endpoint on the opt-in status listener, guarded by the existing HTTP token, and bounded shutdown that closes listeners and accepted client/relay sockets. A guide covers probe results, supervisors and what players lose on restart.
Health is 200 only while both game serving loops are active, 503 during startup/shutdown or after a loop exits. Loopback and subprocess tests cover shutdown; systemd/container restarts and remote failover are not run. Rooms and scores remain in memory and are lost on restart. No database retry is needed until a network backend exists.		available0.4.0
Active/passive failover ha-failover
Docs and example files for a standby server: a floating address (keepalived) or a proxy's health checks, both servers on the same database, one active at a time. No election or replication inside the server.
Not started. After ha-restart; the shared database needs store-postgres or store-mariadb. Live rooms are lost on failover.		plannednot released
Several servers ha-multi
Several servers behind one address, each room wholly on one server, with a routing layer that sends a new room or a join to the right one.
On the back burner: revisited after ha-restart and ha-failover exist and one server is not enough.		laternot released
Live room handover ha-handover
Rooms that survive the loss of a server.
Needs replicated live state; out of scope for a server of this size.		declinednot released

Network

FeatureStatusSince
Address discovery and hole punching net-punch
A player's P2P socket sends the server a UDP PROBE. The server records the public endpoint and gives each viewer the address that works from where they are: the public one from another network, the LAN address from the same one.
Upstream work. The NAT lab runs it in Docker in CI.		available0.2.0
Relay net-relay
-relay, off by default: streams into a player behind a router go through the server, and datagrams go through the server's UDP port when punching does not get through (as with a symmetric NAT).
Upstream work. Uses the server's bandwidth; there is no per-player budget yet (net-guardrails).		available0.2.0
UDP source address check net-udp-guard
PROBE and RELAY packets are accepted only from the IP address of the player's TCP connection. A probe's local_ip is kept only if it is private, carrier-grade NAT, link-local or the probe's own source. -udp-any-source turns the check off.
A Podman run is recorded in docker/README.md.		available0.2.0
More UDP and relay guardrails net-guardrails
Bounded per-source-IP UDP packet admission shared by probes, relay and invalid traffic, plus aggregate drop-reason counters in /api/stats. The token bucket tracks at most 4096 sources, expires idle entries and rejects new sources at capacity.
Initial packet limiter only: default 1000 packets/second with the same burst, configurable with -max-udp-rate and 0 for off; players behind one NAT share it. Per-player relay byte/datagram budgets, payload and TCP stream limits, failed-token blocking and UDP fuzz coverage remain planned. A larger token needs a protocol version bump.		partial0.4.0
Connection checks net-checks
A check for players and hosts that says where a connection fails (server reachable, HELLO accepted, UDP probe answered, NAT behaviour, peer reachable, relay available) and shows round trip, loss and whether each peer is up.
Not designed yet.		plannednot released
UPnP net-upnp
Open a player's P2P port on their router automatically.
Not started.		laternot released

Client

FeatureStatusSince
C client client-c
One file with no dependencies and no threads: psnr_send returns a request id, and psnr_poll hands out replies and pushes; sends and automatic heartbeat writes can wait for socket writability. It also builds the UDP probe and relay packets.
Upstream work. The integration guide documents ownership and timeout limits. TestCClient also compiles/runs the minimal example; it skips without a C compiler, and Linux CI requires execution.		available0.1.0
Go client package app-client
app/internal/client: a Go client for the TCP protocol, for the desktop app. HELLO, heartbeat, create, search, join and leave rooms, record and read scores, and the member and route pushes, with typed messages and errors. re-psn-app check HOST:PORT uses it.
Room data and messages, kicks, invite-only rooms, relay streams and UDP are not in it yet.		partial0.3.0
Desktop app, terminal UI app-tui
re-psn-app with no arguments: a first-run choice of Play, Host or Both with the online ID and the server, a menu and content pane (one at a time under 70 columns), a Status screen with Rooms and Leaderboards tabs over the game protocol or an explicitly configured HTTP status source, a Settings screen that saves re-psn.ini, and a dark or light theme in the website colours. Built on Bubble Tea and Lip Gloss.
Partial: no Host screen, room joining, launch profiles or theme presets yet. Linux desktop starts without a TTY can open a supported terminal; Windows uses its console. Synthetic startup tests ran; physical desktops/emulators remain unverified. The optional HTTP source adds uptime, connection counts, public-room members/age and board leader summaries with bounded authenticated fetches and game-protocol fallback. The game protocol still lacks those extra fields; neither source reports server version. Driven in tmux on Linux; not tried on Windows or macOS terminals.		partial0.3.0
Desktop client, terminal UI client-desktop
A terminal program for players and hosts: launch profiles per game, a host mode, and a check of the connection.
Not started. One executable per platform, with nothing else to install.		plannednot released
Desktop client, graphical UI client-gui
A local web UI served by the same program, and a graphical app on Windows, with the same screens as the terminal UI.
Not started. After client-desktop.		plannednot released
Colour themes app-themes
Colour presets in the desktop apps: gruvbox-material by default, then gruvbox, catppuccin, kanagawa and melange. A preset is a data file shared by the apps and the README art.
Not started. A preset ships only after its project's licence is read and credited in NOTICE.md. The terminal UI falls back to the terminal's own 16 colours and respects NO_COLOR.		plannednot released
Appearance mode app-appearance
Dark, Light or System (the default): presets carry a dark and a light variant where their project has both, and System follows the OS or the terminal background and switches while the app runs.
Desktop presets and system-following remain planned. The server status page supports browser System/Light/Dark and local appearance controls; see status-page.		plannednot released
Custom colours app-colours
Edit named colour slots (background, surface, text, muted, accent, good, warn, bad) as hex values, with a contrast warning below 4.5:1, import and export, saved per user and per mode.
Not started. A bad value falls back to the default preset.		plannednot released

Release

FeatureStatusSince
Release archives and checksums release-archives
scripts/release-build.sh builds static binaries for windows/amd64, linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 into re-psn-vX.Y.Z-<os>-<arch> archives and one SHA256SUMS listing them. A pushed version tag makes a draft pre-release; a second workflow checks a published one.
Published as the v0.2.0 pre-release (2026-11-06): the release workflow and the published-release check both passed. The Windows and arm64 binaries are cross-built and not run.		partial0.2.0
Linux AppImage release-appimage
scripts/build-appimage.sh packs the linux/amd64 server binary and its examples as re-psn-vX.Y.Z-x86_64.AppImage, with appimagetool 1.9.1 and the type-2 runtime 20251108, both downloaded by the release workflow and checked against pinned SHA-256 hashes. A smoke test compares its -h and version with the binary's, and it is listed in SHA256SUMS.
Published in the v0.2.0 pre-release (2026-11-06); the release workflow built it on a runner and passed its smoke test. It was also built and run on one x86_64 Linux machine, with FUSE and with --appimage-extract-and-run. x86_64 only, unsigned.		partial0.2.0
Install scripts install-script
scripts/install.sh (Linux amd64 and arm64, POSIX sh) and scripts/install.ps1 (Windows amd64; written for PowerShell 5.1 and 7, tested on 7 only) install the server for the current user from a GitHub release, newest or pinned, after checking the download against SHA256SUMS. No sudo or administrator rights, no profile edits; --dry-run, --dir, --appimage, -AddToPath.
Partial: release assets (install.sh, install.ps1, listed in SHA256SUMS) since v0.4.0; v0.3.0 does not carry them. The Linux tests run under dash, bash and BusyBox ash with a fake release, and the published v0.4.0 install.sh installed that release on Linux amd64 into a temporary directory; install.ps1 has not installed from a published release. The PowerShell fake-release tests have passed under PowerShell 7 on Linux and Windows CI; PowerShell 5.1 remains untested. No macOS builds, so no macOS support.		partial0.4.0
Release process release-process
Written steps for cutting a release (tag, notes from CHANGELOG.md, checking the draft, publishing), a check that the version in the code and in CHANGELOG.md agree, and a dry run of the release workflow before the first tag.
VERSION, the version check (TestVersionAgrees), scripts/bump-version.sh and scripts/release-notes.sh are built and docs/releasing.md has the steps; the release workflow builds its notes with the notes script and checks that a tag is v + VERSION, and the first tag, v0.2.0 (2026-11-06), ran the whole path: the dry run, the tag step and the draft job passed, and the draft was published by hand after its assets were read back. No fixed release day: while things are worked out, pre-releases (v0.x, marked pre-release) come whenever there is something worth trying.		available0.2.0

Changes

Unreleased

Added

  • HEARTBEAT may carry the player's own last round trip (rtt_ms, 2 bytes).
  • /api/stats and the status page count verified players: each public room has verified (members whose UDP probe the server has accepted on this connection) and the top level has verified_players.
  • -relay-force (RE_PSN_RELAY_FORCE, off by default, needs -relay): every stream goes through the relay, even between players who could connect directly, so the relay can be tested from one network.
  • The status page and /api/stats show known games by name: rooms and leaderboards carry a label such as [Killzone 3 (BCUS98234, BCES01007)], with game and serials fields, and are sorted by it.

Fixed

  • re-psn -h no longer prints the status token.

0.4.0 (2026-11-09)

14 under Added, 3 under Changed.

The full history is in CHANGELOG.md.

Settings

Each of the 22 flags can also be set as a RE_PSN_<FLAG> variable. A flag on the command line wins, then the variable; a value that does not parse stops the server at start. It runs with no settings at all. docs/running.md has the full text.

FlagVariableDefaultWhat it does
-addrRE_PSN_ADDR:36100TCP and UDP address for game clients
-tcp-addrRE_PSN_TCP_ADDR-addrTCP address for game clients, if different
-udp-addrRE_PSN_UDP_ADDR-addrUDP address for game clients, if different
-httpRE_PSN_HTTPnone (off)Status page and /api/stats on this address, for example 127.0.0.1:36101
-http-tokenRE_PSN_HTTP_TOKENnoneToken the status page requires (Authorization: Bearer, or ?token=)
-max-roomsRE_PSN_MAX_ROOMS1000Rooms across all titles
-max-player-roomsRE_PSN_MAX_PLAYER_ROOMS8Rooms one player may be in at once (0: no limit)
-max-conns-per-addrRE_PSN_MAX_CONNS_PER_ADDR32Open connections per remote address (0: no limit)
-max-req-rateRE_PSN_MAX_REQ_RATE200Requests per second per connection before it is closed (0: no limit)
-max-udp-rateRE_PSN_MAX_UDP_RATE1000UDP packets per second per source (IPv4 address or IPv6 /64), shared by probes and relay traffic; same-size burst (0: no limit); since v0.4.0
-vRE_PSN_VoffSame as -log-level debug
-log-levelRE_PSN_LOG_LEVELinfodebug (room events), info, warn or error
-log-formatRE_PSN_LOG_FORMATtexttext or json
-log-fileRE_PSN_LOG_FILEnoneAlso append the log to this file (mode 0600)
-trusted-proxiesRE_PSN_TRUSTED_PROXIESnoneReverse proxies allowed to name the real client (CIDRs or addresses)
-proxy-protocolRE_PSN_PROXY_PROTOCOLoffRequire a PROXY v1/v2 header from a trusted proxy on the game TCP port
-udp-any-sourceRE_PSN_UDP_ANY_SOURCEoffAccept UDP probes and relay packets from another address than the player's TCP one
-relayRE_PSN_RELAYoffCarry traffic for players who cannot reach each other (uses the host's bandwidth)
-relay-forceRE_PSN_RELAY_FORCEoffWith -relay, send every stream through the relay, even between players who could connect directly. For testing the relay from one network; uses the host's bandwidth
-dbRE_PSN_DBoffScore storage: off or memory
-db-fileRE_PSN_DB_FILEnoneRead the -db setting from this file instead
-replaceRE_PSN_REPLACEoffIf an earlier re-psn of this user holds the game port, stop it (SIGTERM) and start in its place (Linux only)

Install

The latest release is v0.4.0, a pre-release.

Release archives

Archives for Linux (amd64, arm64) and Windows (amd64), and a Linux x86_64 AppImage, all unsigned, with a SHA256SUMS file. Check a download on Linux:

sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing

On Windows, compare the output of Get-FileHash <archive> with the line in SHA256SUMS.

Container

docker pull ghcr.io/undecuple/re-psn:0.4.0
docker run --rm -p 36100:36100 -p 36100:36100/udp ghcr.io/undecuple/re-psn:0.4.0

Podman works the same way. See docker/README.md.

From source

You need Go 1.22 or newer; a C compiler only for the C client and its tests.

go build -o re-psn ./server
./re-psn

Connect

Players on one LAN or VPN need nothing forwarded. Otherwise the host forwards a port, runs a public server, or uses an overlay network such as Tailscale or ZeroTier; the relay is the fallback when two players cannot reach each other.

  • Game connection and address probes: :36100, TCP and UDP, open to every player.
  • Status page: none (off), for the host only; it lists every online ID.
  • Each player's P2P port (UDP and TCP) must be reachable by the other players; the game opens it.

A game reaches the server through the C client in client/psnr.c, via ps3recomp's NP modules. That side is upstream's work; docs/connecting.md covers each way to connect.
